prediction:
Issue #73, saturating the VP monitor mix's int16 accumulator plus the instrument that says whether it can ever fire. Judged on soak logcat (hakuX-audio mon_acc:, level: and starve: lines), not on captures: no golden PCM from silicon exists, which is why this stream has no oracle. The accumulation site is vp.c's monitor block; the fix clamps a sum outside +/-32767 instead of letting it wrap.

MECHANISM BEING TESTED, and it corrects the issue's own premise. Voice count cannot overflow this accumulator: voices sum in float (vp.c:1582 per voice, vp.c:1706 across the workers) and convert once through src_float_to_short_array, which clamps to +/-1.0 first. What the += accumulates is 32-sample SLICES of monitor.frame_buf, and the schedule normally puts exactly one value in each: eight slices, index (ep_frame_div % 8), whole buffer flushed and memset at (ep_frame_div + 1) % 8 == 0 (apu.c:692) with apu.c:726 the only increment. The one path left is gp_ep.c:424 setting ep_frame_div = 0 on a guest NV_PAPU_EPRST write without clearing frame_buf; arriving with ep_frame_div % 8 in 1..7 that revisits already-written slices, and two near-full-scale samples of the same sign then suffice.

M1 (CONTROL, not a falsifier) -- the instrument is alive. At least one mon_acc: line per soak with a non-zero window sample count. Zero lines, or zero samples, is a diagnosis: the tag is filtered, the build lacks the counter, or monitor.point is not MON_VP (use_dsp true). It invalidates M2/M3 rather than answering them.

M2 -- THE LEG THAT MATTERS. mon_acc cumulative nonzero == 0 for the whole soak, on both titles. That says the accumulator never accumulates, so #73 is unreachable in practice at this configuration and the clamp is provably inert. FAILS if nonzero > 0, and that failure is the valuable outcome: a title really does resync the EP mid-cycle, the hazard is live, and the frame-sync rewind at gp_ep.c:424 -- not the arithmetic -- is the thing to fix next. NOT forced true by my change: the counter observes a guest register write this patch does not touch, and 7 of the 8 possible arrival phases for an EPRST write would make it non-zero.

M3 -- mon_acc cumulative saturated == 0. Separated from M2 on purpose, because nonzero > 0 with saturated == 0 is a third disposition ("the path runs, it never overflows") needing a different follow-up from either of the others. FAILS if saturated > 0, which would mean the pre-fix code was wrapping and the wrap-suspect counter -- a count of full-scale sign flips in the OUTPUT, a consequence rather than the event -- was missing it.

M4 -- the rewrite did not change the mix. The level meter's median active-window AC RMS stays within 2.0 dB (2000 millidB) of the same-title reference and peak still reaches 32,767 on Galleon. This binds even if M2 holds, and that is its point: the two-statement += became a nested channel loop with isamp[2*i+ch] and frame_buf[off+i][ch], so an index slip is possible and would show here while M2 stayed clean. References: Galleon meter p50 -29.15 / -29.25 dBFS (result 1789279659); Crimson Skies p50 -15.95 / -15.65 dBFS (result 1789280122). FAILS outside 2.0 dB.

M5 -- the counter does not cost the audio thread its deadlines. Every steady-state starve: line reads 0.0000% (0 ppm), startup windows excluded per audio-baseline.md 4a. FAILS on any non-zero steady-state figure, in which case the counter comes out before any of its numbers are quoted.

WHAT M2 CAN AND CANNOT BOUND. About 8.2M samples per 85 s run, but occurrences arrive in bursts of at most 7*32*2 = 448 samples per rewind, so M2 bounds the NUMBER OF EPRST REWINDS during roughly 170 s of two titles' play, not a per-sample rate. A zero is evidence of rarity at this configuration on these titles; it is not proof the rewind cannot happen, and the counter is permanent so every later audio soak adds to it.
